name: Domaine Grand Veneur Châteauneuf-du-Pape Vieilles Vignes 2010
text:
## Grand Veneur Châteauneuf-du-Pape Vieilles Vignes 2010

**Story.** It is the same cuvée as wine 5. In 2010 it was a 4,000-bottle blend of 50% Grenache, 40% Mourvèdre and 10% Syrah from 55- to 105-year-old vines, aged 18 months in small oak. See [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Chateauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k).

**Reviews.** The critics split on this one.
- Jeb Dunnuck: 99 (July 2017, confirmed on his site; he had 98+ on release and called it just now starting to round the corner). Robert Parker (Wine Advocate, Oct 2012): 100.
- Wine Spectator: 93.
- World of Fine Wine: 94.

CellarTracker community score, from your list: 94.8 (2010). That sits much closer to the 93–94 critics than to Parker's 100.

**Practical note.** Parker said 5–6 years of cellaring, then 25–30 years of ageing. Decant for an hour. Try it with lamb tagine or a mature hard cheese.

**Curious aside: two ways of seeing 2010.** Parker called it akin to chewing meat. Wine Spectator's note reads as more reserved, which fits the gap in scores.

### From the history books
- 1791: Avignon and the Comtat Venaissin leave papal control and are absorbed by France (see [Avignon Papacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy)).
- 1936: AOC status (see [Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- 1976: Alain Jaume founds Grand Veneur (see [this search](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Alain+Jaume+Grand+Veneur&go=Go)).

**Sources:** Jeb Dunnuck (subscriber site, checked directly), Uncorked, Falstaff, Farr Vintners, J.J. Buckley, Vinfolio, FRW, First Bottle, Kysela, Benchmark Wine, K&L, Whwc, Thatchers, Winewithseth, CellarTracker, Delectable, closdesspiritueux.com, and Wikipedia ([Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC), [Nahe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahe_(wine_region)), [Vouvray AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_AOC), [La Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape), [Avignon Papacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy), [Great French Wine Blight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_French_Wine_Blight)).
